# Pinterest.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/pinterest-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/pinterest-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects data from Pinterest.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Pinterest in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-pinterest)
- **Code:** [`pinterest.py`](pinterest.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Board](results/board.json) · [Downloads](results/downloads.json) · [Pin](results/pin.json) · [Profile](results/profile.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Pinterest.com search results for pin data including titles, descriptions, images, videos, destination links, board names, and owner usernames
- Pinterest.com boards (`/<user>/<board>/`) for board metadata and their pins
- Pinterest.com profiles (`/<user>/`) for profile metadata and the user's pins
- Pinterest.com pin detail pages (`/pin/<id>/`) for full pin data
- Bulk pin image downloads

## Functions

- `scrape_search(query, max_pages=3)` → `PinSearch`: Scrape Pinterest search results and return parsed pin data.
- `scrape_board(board_url, max_pages=3)` → `BoardScrape`: scrape a Pinterest board's metadata and pins
- `scrape_profile(username, max_pages=3)` → `ProfileScrape`: scrape a Pinterest user's profile metadata and their pins
- `scrape_pin(pin_url)` → `PinDetail`: scrape a single Pinterest pin's details

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import pinterest


async def main():
    search = await pinterest.scrape_search(query="home office desk", max_pages=3)
    board = await pinterest.scrape_board("https://www.pinterest.com/nasa/mars/", max_pages=2)
    profile = await pinterest.scrape_profile("nasa", max_pages=2)
    pin = await pinterest.scrape_pin("https://www.pinterest.com/pin/142567144444540246/")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`PinResult`**: `pin_id`, `url`, `title`, `description?`, `alt_text?`, `image?`, `image_thumb?`, `destination_link?`, `video_url?`, `is_product`, `board?`, `board_url?`, `owner?`, `domain?`, `save_count?`, `created_at?`
- **`PinSearch`**: `query`, `search_date`, `pins`
- **`BoardScrape`**: `username`, `board_slug`, `board_name`, `description?`, `pin_count?`, `follower_count?`, `url`, `pins`
- **`ProfileScrape`**: `username`, `full_name?`, `bio?`, `follower_count?`, `following_count?`, `pin_count?`, `profile_image?`, `url`, `pins`
- **`PinDetail`**: `images`
- **`DownloadResult`**: `pin_id`, `url`, `image_base64?`, `success`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`pinterest.py`](pinterest.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `country` = `"us"`: country of the proxy

## Notes

### How It Works

Pinterest's board and profile pages server-render a resource cache (embedded in
the page's `__PWS_INITIAL_PROPS__` script tag) describing which internal
`/resource/<Name>/get/` feed backs the page. Every page of pins — including the
first — is then fetched from that API, authorized with the `csrftoken` cookie
and `x-app-version` header captured from the same browser session. No login is
required, since this is all public data.

Those feeds are *gated* by default: the request Pinterest's own front end makes
(and the copy cached in the page) returns image-only pin stubs with no title,
description, board or owner. Each call therefore forces `"gated": false` in the
resource options to get the full pin objects back, and the scraper raises if a
page comes back as stubs anyway rather than silently emitting empty pins.

Pin detail pages render client side and expose no resource cache at all, so
`scrape_pin` reads the pin from the `PinResource` API using the same session.
Deleted or private pins quietly redirect to `/ideas/` instead of returning a
404, which `scrape_pin` detects and reports.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/pinterest-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_board_scraping`, `test_profile_scraping`, `test_pin_scraping`, `test_download_images`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
